sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-08-v16-quick/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks C7 row 6; Internal Quality Checks C7 row 6)
qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md (line 15 no hidden requirements, keyboard conventions; line 23 tool feasibility)
task/tests/test.sh (app launch, DB_PATH, copy, restart helper)
evidence: Reachability is fine: Node 22, express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 are supplied via NODE_PATH in both environment/Dockerfile:3-12 and tests/Dockerfile:9,16-22; integration.md:3-11 tells the builder about the start command, a working directory outside /app, PORT, DB_PATH and a writable copy, which matches test.sh:90-112. The seed is empty and says so. All six notes exist and instruction.md says there are six. The fixes from f2e52393 do not add ambiguity. behaviour.md:13 now gives the requester's reason for plain HTTP saves and restores (seeing them in the network panel), and the idempotent-restore wording leaves both a request-key design and a base-revision design valid. Endless-loop termination can be done: the golden instruments loops (runtime.ts:33-53). Preview network denial (security.md:3) is clear enough that a resolved no-cors fetch counts as reaching the network. Two graded behaviours are not stated anywhere in the public notes. REVIEW_POLICY.md:15 says keyboard conventions must be checked against the public instructions, so both count as hidden requirements. (1) Select-all: functional/judge.toml cw_newer_run_supersedes (weight 1.5) requires 'click into the code, select all with the keyboard, type the new line'. No public file mentions select-all or Ctrl+A (grep of environment/ and instruction.md finds nothing). ui.md:5 lists only typing, pasting, Enter, Backspace, Delete, the arrows, Home/End, Ctrl+Home/End and Shift+arrows. The golden does implement it (custom-editor.js:314-316,482), which shows a golden default turned into a grader requirement. (2) Backward wrap in Find: cw_find_forward_backward_wrap requires 'Previous from the first must wrap to the last', but ui.md:11 says only that 'stepping past the last match wraps round to the first', so the stated wrap is forward only. Smaller ambiguity, not counted as blocking: in cw_selection_replace_and_paste_undo the failure clause can be read as needing one Undo after typing over a selection, while ui.md:9 allows character-by-character undo for single-caret typing. Missing evidence: raw-evidence-index.json is absent from the run folder, so no golden or judge run was cited for this row.
counterexample: An editor that follows every line of ui.md but has no Ctrl+A handler. In cw_newer_run_supersedes, Ctrl+A selects nothing in the editor (or selects the page), so the judge's new one-line draft is typed into the old source. The second Run then runs the old timer code as well, the old marker appears after about 4 seconds, and the criterion fails (1.5 weight) for a behaviour the brief never asked for. Separately, an app whose Find Previous stops at the first match instead of wrapping still satisfies ui.md:11 as written but fails cw_find_forward_backward_wrap.
suggested_fix: In ui.md, add select-all ('Ctrl/Cmd+A selects the whole file') to the keyboard list and change the Find sentence to 'stepping past the last match wraps round to the first, and Previous from the first wraps to the last'. Alternatively, change cw_newer_run_supersedes to clear the draft only with behaviours already stated (for example Ctrl+Home then Shift+Ctrl+End, after also stating that), and drop the Previous-wrap requirement. Optionally say explicitly that one Undo is required only for paste-over-selection, not for typing over a selection.
